Ludwig Güterbock (1873-1943) was a prominent German banker and economic figure who played significant roles in German finance during the Weimar Republic era.

## Career Highlights

**Banking Leadership:**
- Served as chairman of the supervisory board of Dresdner Bank, one of Germany's major financial institutions
- Was involved with various other financial institutions and corporate boards
- Considered one of the influential figures in German banking during the 1920s and early 1930s

**Government Service:**
- Briefly served as Reich Economics Minister in 1923 during the hyperinflation crisis
- His tenure was very short (just a few weeks) during the cabinet of Gustav Stresemann
- Attempted to deal with the severe economic crisis Germany was facing at the time

## Historical Context

Güterbock worked during one of the most turbulent periods in German economic history, when the country was dealing with:
- Post-WWI reparations
- The hyperinflation of 1923
- The eventual stabilization of the currency
- The global economic crisis beginning in 1929

## Personal Fate

As someone of Jewish heritage, Güterbock faced persecution under the Nazi regime:
- Forced to resign from his positions after the Nazis came to power in 1933
- Died in 1943, during the Holocaust period

His life and career illustrate both the prominence of Jewish Germans in Weimar-era finance and business, and the tragic fate that befell many of them under Nazi rule.
